question.text: Two blocks <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> of masses <math><mn>3 </mn><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and <math><mn>6 </mn><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> are connected by a massless spring of force constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1800</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and then they are placed on a smooth horizontal surface. The blocks are pulled apart to stretch the spring by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and then released. What is the the relative velocity (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>) of the blocks when the spring comes to its natural length?

solution.text:
Let μ is reduced mass of the two blocks, then

μ=m1m2m1+m2=3×63+6=189=2 kg

Let vr be the relative velocity of the two blocks, then from conservation of mechanical energy we get

12μvr2=12kx2
vr=xkμ=5×10-218002

⇒vr=1.5 m s-1
